title: ASHES vent field dive, Axial Seamount

briefing.summary: Descend about 1,540 m to the ASHES hydrothermal field, a cluster of black-smoker chimneys near the base of Axial Seamount's western caldera wall. Find and scan the Mushroom and Inferno chimneys, then survey the field's smaller vents and the real caldera terrain around them.
facts: Axial Seamount erupted in 1998, 2011 and 2015. Scientists use seafloor deformation and earthquakes to track the magma reservoir between eruptions.

ASHES is one of the only hydrothermal fields on Earth wired for real-time monitoring: the Ocean Observatories Initiative's Regional Cabled Array streams live seismic, pressure, chemistry and HD video data to shore continuously.
ASHES is a compact field of dark sulfide chimneys on fractured basalt, with tubeworms and pale microbial mats around cooler flow.
Mushroom and Inferno, the field's two best-documented chimneys, sit only about 10 m apart -- keep an eye on your position so you scan both without leaving the immediate vent cluster.
hazards: Scalding vent fluid: Mushroom and Inferno vent over 275 degC just centimetres from near-freezing seawater.
Fragile mineral chimneys; keep a respectful distance to avoid damaging delicate spires.
Sunlight fades with depth; use your lights to read the deeper terrain.
Active volcanic terrain: inflation, deflation and eruptions reshape the seafloor.

objectives.title: Locate and scan the Mushroom chimney
objectives.hint: Mushroom, a chimney in the ASHES field, is at the western caldera wall's base, around 1,540 m.

objectives.title: Locate and scan the Inferno chimney
objectives.hint: Inferno, a black smoker, is beside Mushroom in ASHES, near the western wall, around 1,540 m.

objectives.title: Survey the Hell, Phoenix and Virgin chimneys
objectives.hint: The Hell, Phoenix and Virgin chimney group is just east of Mushroom in ASHES, around 1,540 m.

objectives.title: Survey the base of the western caldera wall
objectives.hint: The western caldera wall rises west of ASHES; find its base on the slope near 1,420 m.
